analysis:
Examined all supplied CLI-reference excerpts and the bounded update patch. The change map places edits outside the numbered excerpts: docs/provider/cli-reference.md head 743–747 adds explicit offline rollback, confirmation and drain/force semantics; head 751 onward describes an update lease and watchdog journaled swap, but the patch is truncated. No supplied implementation demonstrates a bypass or other concrete regression. Rollback must be reconciled in integration with T-043, T-013, T-034, T-054 and assets A-011/A-017: verify retained-artifact validation, journal/generation custody, quarantine persistence, and current coordinator qualification after restart. Offline restoration alone is not evidence of authorization bypass.

Surrounding evidence documents fail-closed authorization and model-switch settlement (head 337–385), provider-versus-desktop credential separation (head 102–108), GLM encrypted prefix identity and cache opt-out (head 37–55), and service-removal confirmation (head 263–273). BASE 2146–2166 and 2278–2355 describe token/key storage, runtime paths and environment forwarding; BASE 2403–2521 describes cluster calibration, ownership and retirement contracts. These unchanged descriptions do not establish implementation correctness or new exposure. T-041's account-scoped cache, HMAC metadata and encryption contracts remain relevant, but no cache control change is shown here. The other changed documentation at head 1852 and 1859–1860 is not supplied. Integration should review those edits and the complete rollback implementation before concluding on the PR's update/availability and attestation interactions; this local documentation pass cannot resolve them.
